name: Bukharinism
summary: Bukharinism is the programme of Nikolai Bukharin and the Right Opposition in the mid-1920s Soviet Union: keep the New Economic Policy, build socialism gradually through a mixed economy of state industry, cooperatives and peasant farming, and hold the worker-peasant alliance together under party leadership. It keeps the Bolshevik framework of proletarian dictatorship, a ruling party and world revolution, but rejects forced requisition and forced collectivisation.
scope: The mature Bukharin of 1921-1929 (NEP, the smychka, the dispute with the Left Opposition and with Stalin's turn), taken from his Economic Structure of Soviet Russia (1922), Draft Comintern Programme (1922), Historical Materialism (1921), Tasks of the Russian Communist Party (1926), World Revolution and the USSR (1927) and Notes of an Economist (1928). Excludes the ultra-left War Communism of 1918-20, the jointly written 1919 ABC of Communism as a source, Stalin-era trial confessions and later market-socialist reformers' use of his name.
